title: Why Have Humans Collected Crystals for 780,000 Years? Chimpanzees May Hold the Answer
hook: Wild chimpanzees show a striking pull toward crystals over ordinary stones — hinting that our own ancient fascination began long before crystals had any practical use.
key_points: Chimpanzees showed a strong preference for crystals over ordinary stones, picking them up and inspecting them with unusual curiosity.
Humans have collected crystals for at least 780,000 years, long predating any known practical use for them.
The chimpanzee finding suggests some perceptual or cognitive feature of crystals themselves — not human culture — drives the attraction.
This reframes crystal-collecting as a deep-rooted feature likely shared with a common ancestor, rather than a purely human cultural invention.
content_html: Humans have been picking up and keeping crystals for at least 780,000 years, long before crystals served any practical purpose. A study of wild chimpanzees suggests we may know why.
extra_html: Researchers found that chimpanzees showed a marked preference for crystals over otherwise similar ordinary stones, picking them up, holding onto them, and inspecting them with unusual intensity. Because chimpanzees share this pull despite having no cultural tradition of crystal collecting, the result suggests the attraction isn't a human cultural invention at all — something about the visual or tactile properties of crystals themselves seems to grab attention across species. That reframes humanity's long, otherwise-impractical habit of gathering shiny stones as a much older, deeper-rooted feature, likely present in a common ancestor long before anyone made a necklace out of one.

related.title: Human Evolution
related.hook: We didn't descend from chimpanzees — we share an ancestor with them. From that branching point, our lineage walked upright, grew big brains, and spread across the planet.

related.title: Apes Have Inner Circles Too
related.hook: Chimps and bonobos build friendships much like we do — a tight inner circle of close partners surrounded by a wider ring of looser ties.
